families.title: Android and JVM assurance adapters
families.description: Reviewed offline Gradle contracts with pinned JDK, Gradle, AGP, Kotlin, integrity, ABI, coverage, and device-evidence boundaries.
assumptions: Android SDK and project dependencies are acquired separately into isolated caches before runtime; every adapter invocation is offline.
Device execution is external environmental evidence and is accepted only through fresh canonical observations bound to source and report digests.
JDK 17.0.20.1+1, Gradle 9.1.0, AGP 9.0.1, and Kotlin 2.3.20 are exact reviewed versions.
Project tasks, integrity digests, lockfiles, repository allowlists, resource limits, and device plans are canonical in quality/android-jvm.json.
The project installs the checksum-pinned AWQ Android/JVM wrapper before invoking adapters; AWQ never installs during a check.

contracts.remediation: Review intentional API changes or restore compatibility, then rerun the exact ABI task.

families.title: Documentation quality adapters
families.description: Reviewed offline commands for Markdown structure, local links, and repository-owned prose rules.
assumptions: Documentation inputs are Git-tracked Markdown or text files; declared fixture trees are excluded.
The project keeps Markdown structure and local-link policy in .rumdl.toml.
Vale configuration, styles, vocabularies, and accepted terminology are fully repository-owned.
rumdl link rules are filesystem-only; external URL availability is not checked or claimed.
The project installs the exact reviewed tools before invoking AWQ; AWQ never installs them.

contracts.limitation: Filesystem-only rules validate relative file targets and fragments; they skip external URL availability and absolute site routes unless project policy configures them.
contracts.remediation: Rerun the exact rumdl link contract, then repair the local target, fragment, or reviewed project link configuration.

contracts.limitation: Markdown structure and style rules cannot establish factual correctness, rendering equivalence, link availability, or prose quality.
contracts.remediation: Rerun the exact rumdl style contract, repair the finding, and review any narrow project suppression.

contracts.limitation: Vale enforces only checked-in rules and vocabularies; it cannot judge truth, completeness, intent, or overall writing quality.
contracts.remediation: Rerun Vale with the repository configuration, then repair the prose or narrowly review the owning rule and vocabulary.

families.title: Python quality adapters
families.description: Reviewed offline commands for Python formatting, linting, strict typing, tests, and branch-aware coverage.
assumptions: The repository supports Python 3.12 and declares authoritative tool settings in pyproject.toml.
Unit tests are discoverable below tests with filenames matching test_*.py.
The project installs official wheels for the exact reviewed Ruff, compiled mypy, and C-extension coverage releases before invoking AWQ; AWQ never installs them.
Coverage run executes before coverage report when both contracts are selected.

contracts.version_output:
Coverage.py, version 7.16.0 with C extension
Full documentation is at https://coverage.readthedocs.io/en/7.16.0
contracts.limitation: Coverage execution shows only code reached by the configured unittest discovery suite and does not prove behavioral completeness.
contracts.remediation: Repair failing tests or the project-owned coverage configuration, then rerun the native command.

contracts.version_output:
Coverage.py, version 7.16.0 with C extension
Full documentation is at https://coverage.readthedocs.io/en/7.16.0
contracts.limitation: The report enforces project-owned thresholds against the existing coverage data file and is meaningful only after a matching coverage run.
contracts.remediation: Run the coverage execution contract first, add meaningful tests, and satisfy the checked-in threshold.

contracts.limitation: Static typing covers only files and strictness declared by the repository and cannot prove runtime behavior.
contracts.remediation: Correct typing findings or explicitly refine the reviewed project-owned mypy configuration.

contracts.limitation: Formatting checks deterministic layout only and does not establish correctness or lint cleanliness.
contracts.remediation: Run ruff format with the checked-in pyproject.toml and review the resulting source changes.

contracts.limitation: Lint rules detect configured static patterns but cannot prove runtime correctness or complete security.
contracts.remediation: Repair Ruff findings under the checked-in configuration and review any suppression narrowly.

contracts.limitation: Discovery executes the repository's unittest suite but cannot establish that all intended behaviors or environments are covered.
contracts.remediation: Repair the failing test or implementation and extend project tests when the behavior lacks coverage.

families.title: Rust stable, supply-chain, and advanced evidence adapters
families.description: Reviewed offline Rust 1.93.0 and dated-nightly formatting, lint, test, build, dependency, API, coverage, fixed-run fuzz, and mutation-sentinel commands.
assumptions: Execution is limited to Linux x86-64 with the exact checksum-reviewed Rust 1.93.0 toolchain and Rust supply bundle installed separately.
The workspace owns exact Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, rust-toolchain.toml and .cargo/config.toml files plus each enabled contract's declared policy snapshot.
The toolchain declaration uses the minimal profile and lists Clippy then rustfmt exactly.
Third-party dependencies are already present in the isolated Cargo home from a separate reviewed acquisition step; runtime is locked and offline.
Registry yank observations, the RustSec advisory database and public API baselines are digest-bound and expire or fail closed independently.

AWQ invokes direct regular binaries with isolated target, home, cache and temporary directories; runtime never invokes rustup, a shell, package installation, advisory updates, registry lookups or lockfile updates.
Advanced evidence uses the separate checksum-pinned AWQ bundle with stable LLVM tools, nightly-2026-09-01, cargo-llvm-cov 0.9.1, cargo-fuzz 0.13.2 and cargo-mutants 27.1.0.
Coverage is PR-bounded; fuzz regression is scheduled; mutation sentinels require a trusted host. Open-ended fuzz and broad mutation campaigns are not adapter operations.
Advanced contracts require clean tracked state, exact repository-owned policies, target lists, seed digests and mutation filters; all generated artifacts and build outputs are external and discarded.

contracts.version_output: awq-rust-supply-check 1.0.0 (cargo-deny 0.20.2; cargo-audit 0.22.2; cargo-semver-checks 0.50.0; Rust 1.93.0; advisory-db bf25f6575a93a35f30796c65c0ed91bee7fa19fd)
contracts.limitation: The exact Cargo.lock is checked against a digest-pinned RustSec snapshot valid through 2026-12-07; the result does not cover unpublished advisories, registry yank state, runtime exploitability or other targets.
contracts.remediation: Update vulnerable dependencies or explicitly review the repository-owned advisory policy; refresh the pinned database through an AWQ release before its expiry.

contracts.limitation: A successful optimized host build proves compilation only for the selected workspace and Linux x86-64 host; it does not prove runtime behavior, other features, targets or profiles.
contracts.remediation: Repair compiler failures or the reviewed workspace and lock configuration, then rerun the exact offline release-build contract.

contracts.limitation: Clippy with warnings denied covers the selected workspace and all host targets under the pinned lint implementation; it does not prove absence of defects.
contracts.remediation: Repair the lint or narrowly review project-owned lint policy without weakening the pinned command, then rerun Clippy.

contracts.limitation: Aggregate line reachability for reviewed packages and default features on Linux x86-64 does not prove assertion quality, branch coverage, other features, targets or behavioral completeness.
contracts.remediation: Add focused tests or intentionally review the repository-owned line floor and package selection, then rerun the exact offline coverage contract.

contracts.limitation: Warning-free no-dependency documentation checks local rustdoc generation only; it does not validate prose truth, external links or dependency documentation.
contracts.remediation: Repair rustdoc warnings or source documentation and rerun the exact offline no-dependency documentation contract.

contracts.limitation: rustfmt checks deterministic source layout only and does not establish compilation, lint cleanliness, tests or runtime correctness.
contracts.remediation: Run the pinned formatter on the workspace, review the source changes and rerun the formatting check.

contracts.limitation: This dated-nightly regression executes only the digest-bound seed corpus and fixed run, time, input-length and Linux x86-64 sanitizer bounds; it is not an open-ended campaign or proof of defect absence.
contracts.remediation: Repair the crashing target, review and add a minimized non-sensitive seed, or deliberately revise the bounded target and resource policy.

contracts.limitation: The result covers only the repository-selected packages, files, regex filters and mutation genres under finite single-worker time and resource bounds; surviving unselected mutants and equivalent mutants remain outside the claim.
contracts.remediation: Strengthen tests to catch each retained sentinel or intentionally review the exact package, file, operator, filter and expected-count policy.

contracts.version_output: awq-rust-supply-check 1.0.0 (cargo-deny 0.20.2; cargo-audit 0.22.2; cargo-semver-checks 0.50.0; Rust 1.93.0; advisory-db bf25f6575a93a35f30796c65c0ed91bee7fa19fd)
contracts.limitation: cargo-deny evaluates the locked graph against repository-owned license, duplicate and source policy plus a time-bounded crates.io yank snapshot; it does not establish legal advice or future registry state.
contracts.remediation: Repair the dependency graph or narrowly review deny.toml, then regenerate the exact Cargo.lock registry snapshot through the bounded setup command.

contracts.version_output: awq-rust-supply-check 1.0.0 (cargo-deny 0.20.2; cargo-audit 0.22.2; cargo-semver-checks 0.50.0; Rust 1.93.0; advisory-db bf25f6575a93a35f30796c65c0ed91bee7fa19fd)
contracts.limitation: The comparison covers the selected library's public rustdoc API for default features on Linux x86-64 against one digest-bound baseline; it does not prove behavioral compatibility, private API stability or other feature and target combinations.
contracts.remediation: Restore the documented public API, select the correct release type, or intentionally regenerate and review the pinned baseline from the release being superseded.

contracts.limitation: The pinned host test suite covers only tests and features selected by the workspace defaults; passing does not prove behavioral completeness or cross-target behavior.
contracts.remediation: Repair failing tests or reviewed workspace configuration, then rerun the exact locked offline host test contract.

families.title: Schema and structured-data adapters
families.description: Reviewed offline checks for strict JSON, restricted YAML, JSON Schema metaschemas, and project-owned instance mappings.
assumptions: JSON and YAML inputs are Git-tracked and declared fixture trees are excluded.
The strict YAML profile intentionally rejects flow collections, explicit tags, anchors, aliases, and duplicate keys.
Every JSON Schema uses the .schema.json suffix, declares a supported $schema dialect, and uses fragment-only or repository-relative .schema.json references.
The project replaces the example schema path and compound instance suffixes with one reviewed mapping per contract identifier.
The checksum-pinned wrapper verifies its bundled parser and validator before running; runtime execution never enables HTTP or installs tools.

contracts.limitation: One copied contract validates only its reviewed schema path and compound instance suffixes; format assertions are implementation-defined beyond supported standard formats.
contracts.remediation: Repair the instance or schema, or review a separate uniquely identified mapping for another schema and suffix set.

contracts.limitation: Metaschema and format-assertion checks validate declared schema structure and a confined local reference graph, not instance behavior or schema design quality.
contracts.remediation: Declare a supported dialect, repair the schema or local reference, and keep every referenced schema below the repository root.

contracts.limitation: Strict parsing rejects duplicate keys and non-finite constants but does not establish application semantics or JSON Schema conformance.
contracts.remediation: Repair invalid or ambiguous JSON, then run the owning schema mapping where one exists.

contracts.limitation: The restricted YAML subset trades compatibility for unambiguous parsing and does not establish application semantics or schema conformance.
contracts.remediation: Remove disallowed YAML features or choose a separately reviewed parser contract for a required broader dialect.

families.title: Shell quality adapters
families.description: Reviewed offline commands for ShellCheck analysis, shfmt formatting, and Bats tests.
assumptions: Shell source uses .sh suffixes or executable POSIX-style shell shebangs and is tracked by Git.
The project declares ShellCheck policy in .shellcheckrc and shfmt policy plus ignored fixture trees in .editorconfig.
Bats tests are stored below tests with .bats suffixes and may use Bash-specific test syntax.
The project installs the exact reviewed tools before invoking AWQ; AWQ never installs them.

contracts.limitation: Bats executes the repository test suite under Bash but cannot prove portability, complete behavior coverage, or compatibility with other shells.
contracts.remediation: Rerun the native Bats command for details, then repair the failing test or implementation.

contracts.version_output:
ShellCheck - shell script analysis tool
version: 0.11.0
license: GNU General Public License, version 3
website: https://www.shellcheck.net
contracts.limitation: Static analysis follows each file's declared shell dialect and configured rules but cannot prove runtime behavior or platform portability.
contracts.remediation: Rerun ShellCheck natively for findings, repair the source, and review any project suppression narrowly.

contracts.limitation: Formatting validates deterministic layout under EditorConfig but cannot establish shell correctness, safety, or cross-shell behavior.
contracts.remediation: Run shfmt with the checked-in EditorConfig, review the formatting changes, and rerun the adapter.
